```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse  = TRUE,
  comment   = "#>",
  fig.width = 10, fig.height = 4.5, dpi = 150, out.width = "100%"
)
library(ggPSE)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Basic gradient map

Supply a data frame with element symbols and a numeric column.
`ggPSE()` maps the column to a fill gradient and returns a standard
ggplot2 object.

```{r basic}
battery <- data.frame(
  symbol     = c("Li", "Co", "Ni", "Mn", "Fe", "P", "C"),
  importance = c(0.95, 0.88, 0.75, 0.60, 0.45, 0.40, 0.35)
)
ggPSE(battery, value_col = "importance", legend_title = "Battery relevance")
```

Elements with no data appear in neutral grey. Because the result is
a plain ggplot2 object, you can keep adding layers:

```{r custom-theme}
ggPSE(battery,
      value_col    = "importance",
      color_low    = "#f7fbff",
      color_high   = "#08519c",
      legend_title = "Battery relevance") +
  labs(title = "Critical elements for Li-ion batteries") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5))
```

## Highlighting element groups

`ggPSE_highlight()` is pipe-friendly and can be stacked to show multiple
groups simultaneously.

```{r highlight}
ggPSE() |>
  ggPSE_highlight(c("Li", "Co", "Ni", "Mn", "Fe", "P"),
                  color = "#2166ac") |>
  ggPSE_highlight(c("Nd", "Dy", "Tb", "Pr", "La", "Ce"),
                  color = "#e63946")
```

## Bubble size encoding

When you want a size signal instead of (or alongside) color:

```{r bubble}
supply_risk <- data.frame(
  symbol = c("Li", "Co", "Nd", "Dy", "Pt", "Rh", "In", "Ga"),
  risk   = c(0.62, 0.91, 0.84, 0.88, 0.52, 0.70, 0.78, 0.65)
)
ggPSE_bubble(supply_risk, size_col = "risk",
             bubble_color = "#d73027", legend_title = "Supply risk score")
```

## Country-of-origin badges

`ggPSE_badge()` overlays ISO country codes showing the primary production
country — useful for critical raw materials analysis.

```{r badges}
supply <- data.frame(
  symbol  = c("Li", "Co", "Nd", "Pt", "Cu", "Ni", "Ga", "In"),
  country = c("CL", "CD", "CN", "ZA", "CL", "PH", "CN", "CN"),
  value   = c(0.70, 0.91, 0.85, 0.60, 0.50, 0.55, 0.80, 0.75)
)
ggPSE(supply, value_col = "value",
      color_high = "#b2182b", legend_title = "Criticality") |>
  ggPSE_badge(supply, country_col = "country")
```

## Faceting across conditions

Because `ggPSE()` returns a ggplot2 object, `facet_wrap()` works out of the box:

```{r facet}
set.seed(42)
elements <- c("Fe", "Cu", "Zn", "Ni", "Co", "Mn", "Cr", "Mo", "W", "V")
ph_data  <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(5, 7, 9), function(ph) {
  data.frame(
    symbol = elements,
    value  = pmax(0, pmin(1, rnorm(length(elements), mean = ph / 10, sd = 0.15))),
    pH     = paste0("pH ", ph)
  )
}))

ggPSE(ph_data, value_col = "value", legend_title = "Affinity") +
  facet_wrap(~pH) +
  labs(title = "Oxophilicity across pH conditions") +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
```

## Saving figures

```{r save, eval=FALSE}
p <- ggPSE(battery, value_col = "importance")

ggsave("pse.pdf", p, width = 18, height = 8, units = "cm")        # vector PDF
ggsave("pse.png", p, width = 18, height = 8, units = "cm", dpi = 300)
ggsave("pse.svg", p, width = 18, height = 8, units = "cm")        # web / HTML
```
